description: Suckled by a she-wolf, founders of Rome, and killers of a brother. A myth that puts law and the sacred boundary above blood.

hero.hook: Rome is not born from a gentle pact. It is born from a she-wolf, a sacred furrow, and a murdered brother.

blocks.text: The story of **Romulus** and **Remus** is the founding myth of Rome. It is not a children's tale. It is the story of a double break: a [[vestal virgin]] who breaks her vow of chastity, then a **fratricide** that puts law above blood.
Roman tradition does not hide the crime. It turns it into the bedrock of a city built on the sacred boundary and on the survival of the state, more than on the family.

At Alba Longa, the city of the descendants of Aeneas, the usurper **Amulius** drives out his brother Numitor. To end the bloodline, he forces his niece **Rhea Silvia** to become a vestal. But **Mars**, god of war, lies with her. Twins are born.

blocks.caption: Mars and Rhea Silvia: the divine birth of the twins

blocks.text: Amulius orders them drowned in the Tiber. The river is in flood and sets the cradle down near the **Palatine**, under the fig tree called the [[Ficus Ruminalis]]. A **she-wolf** nurses them, and a woodpecker, the bird of Mars, feeds them. The shepherd Faustulus and his wife Acca Larentia raise them.

blocks.caption: The Capitoline Wolf, image of Rome as orphan and predator

blocks.text: In Latin, “lupa” means she-wolf, and also prostitute. Ancient authors already suggested that Acca Larentia, who carried that nickname, was the real “wolf” of the legend.

As adults, the twins overthrow Amulius and put Numitor back on the throne. Then they want to found a city of their own. Romulus picks the **Palatine**, Remus the Aventine. To settle it they take the [[augurs]]: Remus sees six vultures first, then Romulus sees twelve.

blocks.caption: The Palatine: the hill where Romulus traces Rome

blocks.text: Romulus traces the [[pomoerium]], the sacred furrow of the city wall, and promises death to anyone who crosses it. Remus jumps over it out of defiance. Romulus, or his officer Celer, kills him. Rome is founded on **April 21, 753 BC**, year one of the [[Ab Urbe Condita]] calendar.
April 21 is still the “Natale di Roma.” At noon the sun strikes the entrance of the Pantheon, an effect ancient architects are said to have designed to glorify power.

First problem: the city has no women. Romulus organizes games and invites the neighbors. In the middle of the festival, the Romans carry off the young women: the **Abduction of the Sabine Women**. The **Sabines**, led by Titus Tatius, declare war.

On the battlefield the Sabine women, already mothers of Roman children, step between their fathers and their husbands. The war stops. The two peoples merge. Romulus and Titus Tatius reign together. The Romans take the name [[Quirites]]. Rome becomes a society that absorbs its enemy.

sections.title: The abduction of the Sabine women

blocks.text: After thirty-seven years of rule and the creation of a Senate of a hundred “fathers,” Romulus vanishes during a storm on the Campus Martius. The official version says Mars carried him up to heaven: he becomes the god **Quirinus**. Another version whispers that the senators murdered him.
What remains is the image of [[The Capitoline Wolf]]: an orphan city, fed by wildness, able to turn outsiders into masters of the world.

blocks.text: Founded on a fratricide and an abduction, Rome draws a clear idea from its myth: the survival of the state and respect for the sacred boundary come before ties of blood.
